Open research notebook on idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis (IGH)

Which treatments help a small white spot match the surrounding skin, and does the match last?

Several treatments bring some colour back within four months. No study found so far has checked whether a treated spot still matched the surrounding skin six months after its last treatment.

4 molongest gap between a final treatment and an assessment, IGH rows
9studies extracted (4 more logged as leads)
20evidence rows, one per arm and time point
0rows that measured complete area coverage
0rows that measured a colour match six months after the last treatment

Generated from data/evidence.csv · last updated 27 November 2026

What the first session found

  • Durability is unmeasured. The longest gap between the last treatment and an assessment was four months, after a single freeze. The top grade in that trial was "more than 75% improved", which is not a colour match.
  • Too much pigment is a real outcome. One excimer series left 18 of 200 spots darker than their surroundings. A peel arm produced scars in 3 of 75 spots.
  • Untreated and sham-treated spots also change. Saline needling cut the median count of white spots from 31 to 21. Graders called 18% of untreated spots improved in a laser trial.
  • Nothing new in PubMed. A dated PubMed search returned 20 records since the 2025 review's cutoff and none is a new IGH treatment trial. One comparison study outside PubMed was found.
  • Misalignment can fake fading. In a simulation, placing the outline 0.25 mm off a 2 mm spot reads as 10 to 16% fading when nothing changed.

How to read this site

Every statement carries one of these labels.

Published human finding A result reported in a paper or trial registry, with a link to where the number appears.

Hypothesis A proposed explanation that fits some observations and has not been tested as a treatment.

Simulation A calculation on synthetic shapes. It tests a measuring method and says nothing about patients.

Calculation on published counts Arithmetic on numbers taken from papers, with the assumptions stated.

You can help

Does anyone know of a study or cohort with photographs of the same confirmed IGH spot at least six months after its final treatment? See Open Questions for this and two smaller asks.

This site is research notes, not medical advice. Whether a particular spot is IGH, and whether to treat it, is a question for a dermatologist.

Contributors

  • Ben. Project lead. Framed the question, wrote the starting brief, reviews every change.
  • Claude (AI model, Anthropic). Session of 27 November 2026: source checks, data extraction, simulation code and site build. Rows it extracted carry a verification status and need a human spot-check.

Evidence

Published human finding Everything in this section comes from a paper, an abstract or a registry record. Each row links to its source and says how far it was checked.

Three outcomes are kept apart because papers often blur them.

  • Partial repigmentation: some colour returned. Most studies stop here, usually as "more than 75% improved".
  • Complete area coverage: the whole spot has pigment again. This can still be the wrong shade.
  • Lasting colour match: colour and texture blend with nearby skin at least six months after the last treatment.

Corrections to the starting brief

The project began from a seed brief. Re-reading each source corrected, qualified or confirmed these points.

5-FU study attribution

Brief said
Section 7 presents PMID 37011024 as the publication of Carlos Wambier (Brown).
Source shows
PMID 37011024 is by Samir Arbache and Sergio Hirata (Brazil). Wambier wrote a separate 2018 letter on 5-FU tattooing for IGH and a comment on the Arbache preliminary report.
Effect
The cohort owner for the split-body trial is the Arbache clinic. Outreach should cite each author's own paper.

PubMed records for PMID 37011024 and 29864463

5-FU delivery method

Brief said
5-FU delivered by medical needling.
Source shows
5-FU and saline were delivered with a tattoo machine. 29 patients (28 women). IQRs: 23-37 to 6-18 (5-FU); 24-43 to 16-31 (saline).
Effect
Medians 32 to 12 and 31 to 21 confirmed.

PubMed abstract, PMID 37011024

Cryotherapy trial denominators

Brief said
82.3% of treated spots and 2% of controls; 101 spots assigned.
Source shows
101 lesions: 43 treated, 58 control. 82.3% does not equal any whole number of 43 lesions.
Effect
The evaluable denominator is unknown until the full text is read. The abstract gives no patient count.

PubMed abstract, PMID 27494272; denominator audit

Cryotherapy vs peel

Brief said
Cryotherapy versus chemical peel; 29/75 vs 15/75.
Source shows
Counts confirmed. The peel was 50% trichloroacetic acid. Arms were assigned by alternate allocation, 15 patients each, 5 macules per patient.
Effect
Not randomized. Spots are clustered within 15 patients per arm.

Deoson 2025, Table 1 and Methods

Excimer follow-up

Brief said
Week 16: 83/200 rated >75% improved; 18/200 with persistent hyperpigmentation.
Source shows
Counts confirmed. Sites were mostly lower limbs (72.7%). The paper gives two different follow-up lengths (1 month in Methods, 4 months in Results).
Effect
Time after last treatment is recorded as about 4 weeks, with the inconsistency noted.

Deepadarshan 2023, Table 1 and text

Grafting report

Brief said
Direct IGH report of autologous epidermal grafting.
Source shows
The abstract covers vitiligo, IGH and post-inflammatory leukoderma together, with no counts and no IGH-specific result.
Effect
Kept as an unquantified lead.

PubMed abstract, PMID 3908515

Cultured-epithelium paper

Brief said
Flagged as a tempting false positive.
Source shows
Confirmed: six patients with vitiligo, piebaldism and albinism. No IGH.
Effect
Excluded.

PubMed abstract, PMID 9229096

Before-and-after image pairs

Brief said
The 13 paired before/after cases are vitiligo.
Source shows
Confirmed in Table 1: evaluation set is 13 vitiligo pairs. IGH has 331 classification images from 39 patients and no pairs.
Effect
No IGH before/after image set was found anywhere.

PMC11604898, Table 1

Senescent melanocytes (Ajou)

Brief said
Ajou researchers reported depleted and senescent melanocytes.
Source shows
The 2023 record has no abstract; only its title supports the statement. A 2026 paper from the same group adds ATG7 loss in IGH skin.
Effect
Statement kept at title level; full text needed.

PubMed records PMID 36394380 and 41453137

Spatial tissue abstract

Brief said
Hopkins-Yonsei reported differences in immune-cell neighbourhoods.
Source shows
Confirmed as SID 2024 abstract 858. Paired lesional and non-lesional sections; Phenocycler imaging. Patient count not stated.
Effect
Paired design confirmed; sample size unknown.

SID 2024 abstract book

5-fluorouracil delivered with a tattoo machine · Arbache 2023

Published human finding

Arbache S, Hirata SH. Dermatol Surg 2023;49(6):603-608 · source · PubMed abstract, Methods + Results; ClinicalTrials.gov record

IGH · split-body, randomized, single-blinded · patients: 29 (28 women) · site: limbs (registry describes upper limbs)

5-fluorouracil delivered with a tattoo machine (number of sessions not in abstract)
After last treatment: 30 days

median achromic lesions 32 (IQR 23-37) at baseline to 12 (IQR 6-18); p = .000003

Excess pigment
no adverse events reported
Complete match

median achromic lesions 31 (IQR 24-43) at baseline to 21 (IQR 16-31); p = .000006

Experiments

1. How much fading can a misplaced outline fake?

Simulation Synthetic disks on a uniform background. No patient images. This tests the measuring method only.

A common way to track a spot is to outline it at the first visit and measure the same outline later. If the outline lands slightly off at the second visit, part of it covers normal skin and the spot looks as if it faded.

Simulation Adjust the spot and the placement error. The filled disk is the spot. The dashed ring is the outline as placed at the second visit.

15.9%apparent fading, sharp-edge formula, with nothing changed
10.0%pixel model with blur and noise (run at 2, 3, 5 mm and 0, 0.25, 0.5 mm only)
13%placement error as a share of spot diameter

Check of the starting formula. The seed brief's closed-form result was rebuilt as a pixel image, with each pixel split into 64 sub-pixels, and measured directly.

SpotOutline off byFormulaPixel model (40 px/mm)Gap, points
2 mm0.0 mm0.0%0.8%+0.765
2 mm0.25 mm15.9%15.9%+0.023
2 mm0.5 mm31.5%31.5%+0.008
3 mm0.0 mm0.0%0.5%+0.520
3 mm0.25 mm10.6%10.6%+0.009
3 mm0.5 mm21.1%21.1%+0.004
5 mm0.0 mm0.0%0.3%+0.317
5 mm0.25 mm6.4%6.4%+0.002
5 mm0.5 mm12.7%12.7%+0.005

The two methods agree to within 0.04 percentage points whenever the outline is displaced. With no displacement, the pixel image reads 0.3 to 1.5% lower than the ideal, because edge pixels are part spot and part skin. The formula has no pixels, so it cannot show that.

Five follow-up situations, four ways of placing the outline. Each cell is 200 simulated captures at 20 pixels per mm, with noise and a 0.1 mm blur. The table shows the 0.25 mm displacement; the results file has 0 and 0.5 mm too.

Cells show signed bias ± spread, in percentage points of baseline contrast, at 0.25 mm displacement. Time per measurement on a 256 × 256 image: fixed 0.18 ms, re-registered 4.28 ms, redrawn 3.42 ms.

What the simulation shows:

  • A fixed outline is biased by displacement in every situation. With blur included, 0.25 mm on a 2 mm spot reads as 10% fading with nothing changed. The sharp-edged formula says 15.9%, so the formula is a worst case.
  • Re-registering the outline removes that bias in this simple scene, including when the spot ends up darker than the skin.
  • An outline redrawn around whatever is still light hides shrinkage. A spot that lost half its area reads as a 1 to 4% change in mean contrast. Multiplying contrast by outlined area recovers the loss.
  • A redrawn outline fails completely on a spot that overshoots to dark. All 200 captures were rejected, which is the correct behaviour: it reports a failure and does not return a number.
  • Darkening of nearby skin changes contrast by a third while the spot itself is unchanged. The separately measured reference lightness (down 5 units) is what reveals it.

Limits: one spot, flat uniform skin, no hair, no curvature, no lighting gradient, and registration that has only the spot to lock onto. Real captures will be worse.

Reproduce it. Needs Python 3.9 or later and numpy. Runs in about two minutes.

python3 experiments/alignment.py            # the seed brief's formula, unchanged
python3 experiments/alignment_pixel_sim.py --out data

2. Do spot-level results survive counting patients, not spots?

Calculation on published counts No new data. Counts are taken from two open tables.

Studies treat five spots per person and analyse them as if they came from different people. Spots on one person tend to respond alike. The calculation below shrinks the sample size by a standard design effect for a range of assumed within-person correlations (0 = spots independent, 1 = all spots on a person respond identically).

The advantage of cryotherapy over 50% TCA is clear only if spots within a person are close to independent. At a correlation of 0.25 the interval already includes zero. The true correlation is unknown, and publishing per-patient results would settle it.

Open Questions

The question this project most needs answered

Does anyone know of a study or cohort with photographs of the same confirmed IGH spot at least six months after its final treatment?

Published or unpublished, any treatment, any body site. A clinic archive counts. So does a clear "we looked and have nothing".

One engineering task

Measure how repeatably a phone can re-find and re-measure a 2 to 5 mm dot.

  • Print a matte target with 2, 3 and 5 mm light dots on a mid-tone background, a millimetre scale and a grey reference in the same plane.
  • Take 10 photographs with the phone fully repositioned each time. Repeat on a second day and, if possible, a second phone.
  • Report two numbers per dot size: how far the registered outline lands from the true centre (mm), and the spread of measured contrast (% of baseline).
  • Compare with the simulation's prediction. Done means a results CSV in the same column layout as alignment_results.csv and the capture settings used.

No skin and no patient images are involved.

One biology question

In biopsies of a white spot and nearby normal skin from the same person, are the pigment cells in the spot missing, or present but holding pigment they are not passing to neighbouring cells?

The two answers point to different repairs. If cells are missing, a treatment has to bring cells in. If cells are present, it has to restart delivery. Anyone with paired sections stained for melanocytes and for melanin could answer this by counting within each patient.

Hypotheses under comparison

Hypothesis None of these has been tested as a treatment in people.

Some spots keep melanocytes that make pigment but hand it over poorly.

hypothesis
Observation
Cultured melanocytes from six IGH patients were larger with short, retracted dendrites and held more melanin than cells from six controls; p16, p21 and hp1 were higher in lesional skin.
Would weaken it
Paired tissue showing melanocytes are simply absent, with no pigment build-up inside the cells that remain.

Rani et al., Int J Dermatol 2018, doi:10.1111/ijd.13960 (abstract checked)

Regaining pigment depends on how many working pigment cells remain or can be recruited.

hypothesis
Observation
After gentle freezing, repigmented spots had more dopa-positive melanocytes than untreated spots but fewer than normal skin. A 2023 letter is titled 'Melanocytes in IGH disappear and are senescent'.
Would weaken it
Baseline biopsies that fail to predict which spots respond. No archive linking baseline tissue to later outcome has been found.

Ploysangam et al., J Am Acad Dermatol 1990, PMID 2229495 (abstract checked); Kim TH et al., J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol 2023, PMID 36394380 (no abstract; title only)

Local tissue changes under the spot help explain why neighbouring skin behaves differently.

hypothesis
Observation
Superficial dermal fibrosis in 18 of 20 paired biopsies. A conference abstract reports more dendritic cells and M2 macrophages and fewer T cells in lesional than paired non-lesional sections.
Would weaken it
The same differences appearing in sun-damaged skin without spots, which would make them a marker of damage and not a cause.

Arbache et al., Int J Dermatol 2022, PMID 35114009 (abstract checked); Alphonse et al., SID 2024 abstract 858 (abstract checked; patient count not stated)

Early loss of the autophagy protein ATG7 drives melanocyte ageing in sun-exposed skin.

hypothesis; added in this update
Observation
ATG7 was reduced in UVB-aged melanocytes and in IGH skin; metformin restored autophagy and delayed senescence in cultured cells.
Would weaken it
No human treatment data exist. A finding in cultured cells says nothing yet about repigmenting an existing spot.

Kim JC et al., Br J Dermatol 2026;194(5):879-887, PMID 41453137 (abstract checked)

Three ways one contributor could help

1. Repeat photography of small spots, built as a follow-up measurement kit

Real owner or dataset
No IGH repeat-capture dataset exists. Design references: Jabour 2025 (vitiligo targets 2-20 cm2), Cronin 2023 (distance and angle). Possible later partners: Anhui image set, Seoul photoacoustic pilot.
Confirmed contents
Simulation in this repository; two method papers read at abstract level
Access today
Fully independent. No patient data needed.
Seven-day result
Printed matte target with 2, 3 and 5 mm dots, scale and grey reference; 10 repositioned captures on 2 days with 2 phones; report alignment error in mm and contrast repeatability, set against the simulation's prediction.
Could change
Gives any clinician with a treated cohort a tested way to re-photograph the same spots at six months. That follow-up visit is the experiment the field is missing.
Main risk
A printed dot is not skin. Hair, curvature and tanning are untested until someone photographs real forearms under consent.

2. Reanalysis of existing treatment outcomes

Real owner or dataset
Arbache split-body trial (29 patients; registry says no individual data sharing); open tables in Deoson 2025 and Deepadarshan 2023
Confirmed contents
Only summary tables are public. No dataset with visits after treatment stopped was found.
Access today
Published tables today; anything patient-level needs an owner to say yes.
Seven-day result
A two-page note: the gap map, the denominator audit, the clustering sensitivity result and a minimum follow-up reporting template.
Could change
Shows investigators which single added visit and which three reported fields would make their next paper answer the durability question.
Main risk
Without patient-level data the reanalysis cannot estimate durability, only show that it is unmeasured.

3. Paired affected and unaffected tissue

Real owner or dataset
Johns Hopkins-Yonsei spatial profiling (SID 2024 abstract 858); Arbache paired biopsies (20 patients); Ajou senescence work
Confirmed contents
Paired design confirmed in two sources. Patient count for the Hopkins set is not stated. No public raw data confirmed.
Access today
None. All three need an invitation.
Seven-day result
A one-page hypothesis matrix with a pre-specified within-patient analysis plan (patient as the unit; robustness to segmentation and region choice), sent with one question.
Could change
Could separate 'cells are gone' from 'cells are present but not delivering pigment', which decides whether to stimulate, transplant or protect.
Main risk
Highest scientific value and lowest access for an outside contributor.

Recommendation. Build the measurement kit first and offer it to a team that already has treated patients. The missing experiment in this field is a visit six months after treatment stops, and a clinician is more likely to add that visit if the photographs can be compared reliably.

Who holds relevant data

Progress Log

27 November 2026 · Session 1

Contributors: Ben (brief, question, review), Claude (checks, extraction, code, site).

Done

  • Re-read every numerical claim in the seed brief's evidence ledger against PubMed abstracts or open full texts. Ten points were corrected, qualified or confirmed; they are listed under Evidence.
  • Identified the anchor review: Aravindakshan and colleagues, Clinical and Experimental Dermatology 2025, 50(9):1741-1747. It searched to November 2023, included 20 studies and states that follow-up data on how long repigmentation lasts are scarce.
  • Ran three dated PubMed queries and one ClinicalTrials.gov query. PubMed returned 20 records since December 2023 and none is a new IGH treatment trial. The registry lists two IGH trials in total.
  • Built the evidence table: 20 rows from 13 studies, each with timing after the last treatment, excess pigment, scarring and a verification status.
  • Checked the "before and after" image claim. The 13 pairs in the Anhui dataset are vitiligo. No IGH before-and-after image set was found.
  • Reproduced the seed brief's alignment formula, confirmed it with an independent pixel model, and extended it to fading, shrinking, dark overshoot and darkening of nearby skin.
  • Ran two calculations on published counts: a clustering sensitivity analysis and a denominator audit.
  • Built this site from Markdown and CSV files with one build script.
  • Added a validator that rejects any evidence record whose numbers lack a verbatim quote, and wrote role definitions for searching, extracting and verifying in later sessions.

Not done

  • Full texts behind paywalls were not read. Rows that rest on an abstract say so.
  • Web of Science, Scopus and data repositories (GEO, BioImage Archive, Zenodo, Figshare) were not searched.
  • The registry-posted results of the excimer pilot were not extracted.
  • No row has a stored verbatim quote yet; re-extraction with quotes is the first task of the next session.
  • Open-access PDFs were read by an automated extractor. Their numbers need a human spot-check against the tables.
  • Nothing has been sent to any researcher. The site is not deployed.

Next

  • Print the dot target and run the repeatability task.
  • Read the free full text of the tip cryotherapy trial to resolve its denominators and patient count.
  • Decide where corrections should be sent, then publish.

Research notes, not medical advice. Published findings, hypotheses and simulations are labelled separately. No patient images are stored or accepted here.
